title: Spanning Tree Protocol and loop prevention

videos.script: Two switches, two cables between them. It looks safer than one. {{two-cables}} It is the fastest way to take a network down. A switch floods a broadcast out of every port, and an Ethernet frame has no counter that runs out. So with a loop in the cables, one broadcast goes round forever, and every lap makes more copies. {{storm}} In this lesson you will close a loop of three switches for three seconds, and watch one port count more than two hundred thousand frames that nobody sent. {{counters}} Then you will switch on the Spanning Tree Protocol. The switches elect a root, and each cable gets one end that forwards. One port in the triangle stops forwarding, and the loop is gone. {{election}} You will read the election in the switches' own files, move the root on purpose, and pull a cable while a ping runs. Half a minute of that ping is lost, and you will see why. {{failover}} Last, you will see how faster versions of the protocol work, and how a port protects itself from a switch somebody plugs in under a desk. {{guard}}
